record.original_question: Let G be a graph that admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time tau, meaning that all entries of the mixing matrix M(t) = U(t) o U(-t) are equal at t = tau, or equivalently that all entries of U(tau) = exp(i tau A) have the same absolute value. Prove that every eigenvalue of U(tau) is a root of unity.

evidence.quote: We say that G admits instantaneous uniform mixing (or simply uniform mixing) at time τ if all entries of M(τ ) are equal. Equivalently, G admits uniform mixing at time τ if all entries of U(τ ) have the same absolute value.
3.1 Open Problem. If G admits uniform mixing at time τ , then the eigenvalues of U(τ ) are roots of unity.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph with adjacency matrix $A$, and consider the continuous-time quantum walk on $G$ defined by the family of unitary matrices
$$U(t) = \exp(i t A), \qquad t \in \mathbb{R}.$$
The mixing matrix at time $t$ is defined entrywise by
$$M(t) = U(t) \circ \overline{U(t)} = U(t) \circ U(-t),$$
where $\circ$ denotes the Schur (entrywise) product. We say that $G$ admits instantaneous uniform mixing at time $\tau > 0$ if every entry of $M(\tau)$ equals $1/|V(G)|$; equivalently, if every entry of $U(\tau)$ has the same absolute value $1/\sqrt{|V(G)|}$.

Prove or disprove the following: whenever $G$ admits instantaneous uniform mixing at some time $\tau > 0$, every eigenvalue of the unitary matrix $U(\tau) = \exp(i \tau A)$ is a root of unity.
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture is stated as an open problem in recent surveys on continuous-time quantum walks. While it is known to hold in all examined examples (e.g., integral abelian Cayley graphs, where Kronecker's theorem yields the conclusion under integrality assumptions), no general proof is known and there is no simple combinatorial explanation linking uniform mixing to the eigenvalues of $U(\tau)$ being roots of unity.

status_evidence.title: Selected Open Problems in Continuous-Time Quantum Walks
status_evidence.snippet: If G admits uniform mixing at time τ, then the eigenvalues of U(τ) are roots of unity.
status_evidence.claim: Stated as an open problem in a recent survey on continuous-time quantum walks.

status_evidence.title: Uniform mixing on integral abelian Cayley graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Using Kronecker's theorem, the time at which an integral abelian Cayley graph has uniform mixing corresponds to eigenvalues that are roots of unity.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results confirm the conjecture in special families (integral abelian Cayley graphs).

status_evidence.title: Uniform Mixing and Association Schemes
status_evidence.snippet: In all known cases of uniform mixing, the eigenvalues of exp(iτA) are roots of unity, but no general explanation is known.
